decisions.decision: Expose fraud scores through a REST prediction microservice
decisions.context: Authorization needs a synchronous scoring interface that returns within tens of milliseconds. The serving interface dimension requires a choice before runtime communication strategy.
decisions.rationale: Choose the API-backed prediction service for direct authorization integration. Sources including “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” support this pattern; the checked design point and its gRPC rival were both unattested, with no warnings.
consequences: Keep inference on the synchronous request path.
Measure end-to-end latency against the actual budget.

decisions.context: The service must continue handling transaction traffic during peaks. Independent request handling allows capacity to grow by adding serving replicas.
decisions.rationale: Choose stateless replicas to preserve synchronous scoring while scaling capacity. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” supports stateless serving; the design point reported no warnings, though the full combination was unattested.
consequences: Keep durable feature state outside serving instances.
Define health checks and capacity limits.

decisions.context: Transaction volume peaks require additional serving capacity, while fixed capacity can leave the service unable to handle demand. The design space supports automatic resource scaling but does not specify a scaling policy.
decisions.rationale: Choose elastic scaling to address peak demand; profiling is useful for sizing but does not provide capacity by itself. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” support elastic scaling. The checked primary point was unattested and had no warnings.
consequences: Set scaling thresholds against measured latency and load.
Keep enough warm capacity to meet the response budget.

decisions.decision: Deploy the model as a real-time service
decisions.context: Each transaction needs a fraud score before authorization, so inference must be available online. A model service separates scoring from the payment application.
decisions.rationale: Choose a real-time model service to provide online scoring while keeping the model separately deployable. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “Three Levels of ML Software” support this deployment approach; the checked point had no warnings but was unattested.
consequences: Include service communication in the latency budget.
Operate the model service as a critical authorization dependency.

decisions.decision: Track model, feature, and dataset lineage across the lifecycle
decisions.context: Auditors need to determine which model version and features produced a score. Lifecycle traceability links models and datasets to their training and deployment context.
decisions.rationale: Choose lifecycle traceability because artifact version alone does not establish the feature and dataset context needed to reconstruct a score. “MLOps Principles” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” support integrated lineage. The checked design point had no warnings but was unattested.
consequences: Persist model version and feature provenance with each score.
Retain lifecycle metadata for the required audit period.

decisions.decision: Serve online features from paired online and offline stores
decisions.context: The scorer needs quick access to features during authorization, while training and audit reconstruction need durable feature data. The paired-store option covers both access patterns.
decisions.rationale: Choose paired stores to support low-latency inference and preserve features for training and later reconstruction. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It (from a Data Scientist Perspective)” support this pattern. The checked point had no warnings but was unattested.
consequences: Define feature freshness and consistency rules.
Record the feature values or immutable feature references used for each score.

uncovered: Score-level explanation format and method for auditors.
Feature computation and point-in-time reconstruction semantics.
Latency SLO percentile, timeout, and overload behavior.
Peak capacity targets and failover scope.
Audit retention, access controls, and tamper resistance.
